A working build-flow ingredient stepper with single-select radio rows and multi-select checkbox rows, plus a segmented step-progress bar
A rewards points ring, foil-texture hero banner and persistent running-total footer, each matching the source app's motion and elevation rules
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in fast-casual restaurant ordering apps and has shipped build-your-own-meal flows at scale.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles: canvas cream #FFF5E1, surface white #FFFFFF, pressed cream #F4E8D0, hairline divider #E8DCC4, text primary (espresso) #451400, text secondary (milk-chocolate) #8A6B4F, text tertiary #B49A82, brand action red #A81612, red pressed #8C1210, red tint wash #F4E2E1, warm tan accent #AC8C5B, foil gradient #D9D4C9 to #A8A296, success green #3C7A3C, spice/hot indicator orange #E07B26. No pure black is ever used for text.
Type ladder: display headers in a bold condensed grotesque (Archivo / Archivo Narrow) set in ALL CAPS at weights 700-800 with 0.3-0.8pt positive tracking (hero 32pt, screen title 26pt, section header 18pt); body and item names in a calmer sentence-case humanist sans (Avenir Next) at weights 400/700, 15-17pt, 0pt tracking; all prices/calories/points use tabular figures.
Spacing/radius: 4pt base spacing unit (scale 4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-54); buttons and cards use a squared 8pt corner radius (never a full pill); bottom sheets use 12-16pt; only progress segments, badges and circular icons use pill/circle radii. Shadows are warm-tinted (mixed from the espresso ink, never pure black): card lift ~2px/6px, footer raise ~4px/14px, sheet ~8px/30px.
Distinctive UI patterns: (1) a sectioned, scrollable build-your-own stepper grouped by RICE/BEANS/PROTEIN/TOPPINGS/SALSAS with single-select radio rows and multi-select checkbox rows; (2) a slim segmented step-progress bar that slides its fill forward as the build advances; (3) a circular rewards-points ring with a conic progress arc and a counting-up center number; (4) a brushed-metal 'foil' gradient hero reserved for featured items only; (5) a persistent running-total footer pinned above the flow with the primary action button.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Reserve the brand red exclusively for actionable or selected elements (primary CTA, selected ingredient check, active tab, rewards fill) — never use it for decorative text or backgrounds.
2. Set every header and button label in ALL CAPS with positive letter-spacing; keep every body string, ingredient name and description in calm sentence case — the contrast between the two is the entire brand voice.
3. Never use pure black anywhere; all text and ink-derived shadows resolve to the espresso brown or a tint of it.
4. Keep every corner radius on interactive surfaces at a squared 8pt by default — reach for a pill shape only on progress segments and count badges, never on primary buttons.
5. Any build/configuration flow must render as a single continuously scrollable list grouped into labeled sections, never as a stack of disconnected screens, and must keep a segmented progress indicator visible throughout.
6. Keep a running price total visible at all times during a multi-step configuration flow — never let the user lose sight of the cost while customizing.
7. Use tabular (monospaced) figures for every price, calorie count, and points value so columns of numbers align cleanly.
8. Animate selection state with a spring (not a linear ease) and pair it with a light haptic tick, so choosing an option feels tactile rather than instant.
9. Treat any metallic/foil-style gradient background as a rare, hero-only accent — never apply it to routine list rows or cards.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App/product name: [insert app name]
- Core transactional flow (e.g. build-a-meal, book-a-table, subscribe): [insert]
- Primary configurable object and its sub-choices (e.g. base, protein, toppings): [insert list]
- Loyalty/rewards mechanic, if any (points, tiers, freebies): [insert or 'none']
- Primary brand color and what it should represent: [insert hex + role]
- Screens needed for this deliverable (e.g. home, build flow, cart, rewards): [insert]
- Target iOS deployment minimum and any accessibility requirements: [insert]
- Any existing brand assets or fonts to substitute for Archivo/Avenir: [insert or 'use defaults']
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete `Color` and `Font` SwiftUI extension file implementing the token ladder above, adapted to the project's own brand hex values where supplied.
2. A reusable section-header component (ALL CAPS label + divider rule) and a build-flow ingredient/option row component supporting both single-select and multi-select states.
3. A persistent bottom footer view combining a live running total with the primary CTA button, including its pressed/disabled states.
4. A step-progress-bar component that visually advances as the user completes each configuration section.
5. If a loyalty mechanic is specified: a circular progress-ring component with an animated conic arc and a counting-up center value.
6. A short SwiftUI preview harness wiring all components together into one working build-flow screen.
7. A one-paragraph rationale explaining any deviation you made from the reference data and why.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in single-brand-color marketplace apps for food delivery.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles: canvas white #FFFFFF (dark canvas #121212, never pure black), surface #F4F4F2, surface pressed #EAEAE8, divider #E8E8E6, text primary #1D1D1B, text secondary #6B6B6B. The single brand/interactive color is a saturated teal #00CCBC, pressed state #00A99C. Content sitting on a teal fill uses a deep teal-ink color #003733 rather than white — this on-teal ink is the signature rule of the whole system. A soft mint #C4F4EF supports a membership panel; a warm gold #FFC100 is reserved strictly for percentage-off promotional badges, never for anything else.
Type ladder: one geometric grotesque (Inter as the closest open substitute) run heavier than typical peers — screen titles at 32pt weight 900 with tight negative tracking (-0.6pt), section headers 22pt weight 800, card names 16pt weight 800, body 15pt weight 500, all prices/fees tabular and bold (weight 800).
Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit; corner radii scale from list thumbnails (8pt) through card photos (12-14pt) to bottom sheets (16pt), while every button, the search field, and the fee pill are a fully-rounded 999px pill. Elevation is nearly flat everywhere — restaurant cards and category tiles carry no shadow at all; shadow appears only on floating actionable elements (a soft ~2px/8px lift).
Distinctive UI patterns: (1) a small rounded delivery-fee chip on every restaurant card pairing a moped/scooter glyph with the fee and order minimum; (2) a floating circular '+' button hanging off the bottom-right corner of a menu-item thumbnail that morphs into an inline quantity stepper on tap; (3) a sticky basket bar that slides up from the bottom embedding the live item count and running total; (4) a horizontally-scrolling row of rounded-square category tiles whose active state inverts to a solid teal fill; (5) a membership banner and badge that intentionally reuse the one brand teal rather than introducing a second membership color.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Use exactly one saturated brand accent for every interactive and brand surface — logo, buttons, active tab, ratings, membership marks, floating add button — resist introducing a second competing accent color anywhere in the chrome.
2. Wherever content sits directly on a fill of the brand accent, use the dedicated dark 'ink' color rather than white — this is the single most identity-defining rule in the system and must never be broken for legibility shortcuts.
3. Never crop or tint hero/menu photography to a square — keep it wide and full color; photography and section spacing (not borders or shadow) are what separates cards from the canvas.
4. Every restaurant/merchant card must surface a compact fee/minimum chip with a leading vehicle or delivery glyph — this is the signature trust-and-cost signal and should never be omitted.
5. Represent the primary 'add to order' gesture as a small floating circular button anchored to a photo's corner rather than a full-width row button — it should morph into a stepper control on first tap.
6. Reserve any secondary promotional color strictly for percentage-off deal messaging — never let it bleed into general chrome or branding.
7. Round every button, chip, and the search field to a fully-rounded pill; reserve square/rounded-rect radii for photography and containers only.
8. Keep shadows almost entirely absent from static list content — apply elevation only to things that are genuinely floating and tappable, such as a sticky summary bar or an active sheet.
9. Embed the running count and subtotal directly into the sticky action bar's label rather than showing them as separate elements.
</house_rules>

- Core marketplace vertical (restaurant delivery, grocery, retail, etc.): [insert]
- Primary brand accent color and any secondary promotional color: [insert hex values]
- Card/list content type (e.g. restaurant, store, provider) and its key metadata fields: [insert]
- Membership/subscription program name and its perks, if any: [insert or 'none']
- Screens needed for this deliverable (e.g. feed, detail/menu, basket, tracking): [insert]
- Target iOS deployment minimum and dark-mode requirement: [insert]
- Existing brand font, if different from the Inter substitute: [insert or 'use default']
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color/Font SwiftUI token extension implementing the single-accent system, including the on-accent 'ink' content color rule.
2. A merchant/restaurant card component with photo, badge, saved-heart, rating row, and the fee/minimum pill.
3. A menu-item row component with a floating circular add button that visibly morphs into a quantity stepper.
4. A sticky bottom action bar component that slides in and embeds a live count + total.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in high-throughput quick-service-restaurant ordering apps with live order-tracking experiences.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles: canvas white #FFFFFF, surface #F4F4F4, surface deep #EAEAEA, divider #E2E2E2, text primary #1F1F1F, text secondary #6E6E6E, text tertiary #9A9A9A. Two brand accents split by strict role: action red #E31837 (pressed #C2122E, tint wash #FCE7EB) for anything the user does — order, build, deals, the active tracker stage — and informational blue #006491 (pressed #00547A, tint wash #E0EEF4) for anything the user reads or that is already complete — links, completed tracker checkmarks, secondary informational buttons. Semantic support: success green #1E8E3E, warning amber #F5A623, unfilled tracker rail #E2E2E2.
Type ladder: a single sturdy grotesque (Archivo, falling back to Helvetica) at weights 400/700 only — no thin or delicate weights anywhere. Screen titles 26pt/700, a large current-stage headline at 22pt/700, item names 17pt/700, prices 16pt/700 tabular, body/description 15pt/400, secondary meta (ETAs, calorie counts) 13pt/400 in the secondary gray.
Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit (scale 4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-52); buttons and cards use a squared 8pt radius as the practical default; the hero tracker card and sheets step up to 12-16pt; only progress/status pills and circular tracker nodes are fully rounded. Shadows are soft and neutral (mixed from the dark text ink, never colored) — cards lift ~2px/6px, the tracker hero and sticky footer lift ~4px/14px, sheets ~8px/30px.
Distinctive UI patterns: (1) a five-node horizontal tracker rail (prep, bake, box, quality-check, out-for-delivery) where completed nodes turn blue with a checkmark, the active node turns red and pulses, and upcoming nodes stay hollow gray; (2) a live build-your-own preview graphic (e.g. a circular pie) whose visual layers update in real time as size/base/topping selections change; (3) bold red-bordered deal tiles with an oversized tabular price callout; (4) a small two-color logomark motif reused as a decorative corner accent; (5) a persistent quantity-control group styled as a bordered '−  n  +' row rather than a pill.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never mix the two brand accent roles — red is exclusively for actions and the currently-active state; blue is exclusively for informational content and already-completed states. Getting this backwards breaks the whole color logic of the app.
2. Keep every button and card corner at a squared 8pt radius by default — reserve fully-rounded pill shapes only for status badges and the circular nodes of the order tracker.
3. Render any multi-stage fulfillment process as a horizontal rail of discrete nodes connected by a fill-able track, not as a plain text status line — this is the product's signature moment and should dominate the screen it appears on.
4. Any live-configurable product must show a real-time visual preview that updates layer-by-layer as options are chosen — never leave a static image while the user customizes.
5. Use weight, not size, to carry hierarchy — titles, item names, prices and buttons are all bold (700); avoid introducing lighter weights purely for visual variety.
6. Every price, ETA, and order total must render in tabular figures so multi-digit numbers stay aligned in lists and totals.
7. Keep the canvas bright white with no tinting — this app's whole visual identity depends on a bright, high-contrast catalog rather than a moody or dim palette.
8. Give the active/current stage of any tracked process a subtle looping pulse animation so it reads as 'in progress' at a glance.
9. Use a neutral, dark-ink-tinted soft shadow (never a brand-colored shadow) for elevation — the brightness of the canvas, not colored glow, should carry visual structure.
</house_rules>

- Deal/promotion format to support, if any: [insert or 'none']
- Screens needed for this deliverable (e.g. menu, build flow, tracker, deals): [insert]

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in high-conversion e-commerce and food-delivery marketplaces optimized for rapid checkout.
</role>

<reference_data>

Titles run 20-28pt weight 700 with tight negative tracking (-0.2 to -0.5pt); merchant names 18pt/700; body 15pt/400; any price is never lighter than weight 700, ranging 15-20pt, always tabular.
Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit (scale 2-4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-56-72); corner radius scales deliberately with commitment level — small tags 4pt, thumbnails 8pt, standard cards 12pt, full-width cards 16pt, secondary pill buttons 20pt, and the primary checkout CTA at the roundest 28pt. Elevation is used to signal 'tap this': merchant cards in a carousel get a light lift (~4px/12px), while the floating checkout button gets the heaviest shadow in the app (~8px/24px) — deliberately heavier than any card.
Distinctive UI patterns: (1) content-intent horizontal carousels ('fastest near you', 'zero fee', 'order it again') stacked vertically, each card deliberately cropped ~30% at the trailing edge to signal more content; (2) a bottom-pinned floating checkout pill that never disappears once the cart has items, showing the label and live total together; (3) merchant cards built around a 16:9/16:10 hero photo with a save-heart in a translucent scrim circle; (4) a horizontally-scrolling category-tile row using square photo icons rather than plain glyphs; (5) live order-tracking with a rounded map panel, a floating driver-avatar card overlapping its edge, and a red route polyline.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Reserve the brand red strictly for elements the user should tap to spend money or commit — never apply it to decorative text, icons, or non-interactive labels.
2. Every merchant/product card must carry a real photograph at a wide aspect ratio (16:9 or 16:10) — never ship a gray placeholder block or a cropped-to-square image.
3. Render every price in bold weight at minimum — money is never displayed in a light or regular weight, and never italicized.
4. Keep the floating checkout/cart button pinned to the bottom of the screen the instant the cart is non-empty, and give it the single heaviest shadow anywhere in the UI — it is the most valuable tap target in the product.
5. Scale corner radius with commitment level: small tags and chips stay closer to square, ordinary cards round moderately, and the final commit-to-purchase button gets the roundest treatment in the whole system.

7. Limit semantic accent colors to exactly two beyond the brand red (e.g. a rating color and a savings/fee-waiver color) — do not introduce additional decorative hues.
8. Keep dark mode a warm near-black rather than true black, and never desaturate food photography in dark mode — only chrome should darken.
9. Use weight 700 for all titles, weight 600 for secondary/tertiary actions, and weight 400 only for prose — never introduce a thin or a black/900 weight.
</house_rules>

Color roles: canvas white #FFFFFF, surface #F6F7F8, divider #E8E9EB, text primary #242529, text secondary #72757E, text tertiary #A6A8AE. Primary action green #0AAD0A (pressed #098F09, tint wash #E6F6E6) drives every add button, the stepper, the cart bar, and active tab state. A carrot-orange #FF7009 (tint wash #FFF0E6) is reserved strictly for deal flags and sale pricing — never for a primary action. A separate sale/error red #D6203A appears only for strikethrough original pricing and error states.
Type ladder: one clean grotesque (Inter) at weights 400/600/700, tuned deliberately compact for a dense scrolling list: store names 17pt/700, product titles 15pt/400 with a hard two-line clamp, prices 15pt/700 tabular (rendered in orange when on sale), unit-price/meta 13pt/400 in secondary gray. No hero display type — the product grid itself is the headline.
Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit (scale 4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-56); most interactive surfaces (buttons, product photos, the stepper, the search field, the cart bar) use a comfortable 12pt corner radius, while filter chips and the compact 'Add' button are a full pill. Shadows are soft, low-opacity and cool-neutral rather than warm or colored — the cart bar gets the most prominent lift (~4px/12px) of anything in the app; product cards barely lift at all, relying mostly on dividers and spacing.
Distinctive UI patterns: (1) a quantity stepper that starts life as a compact outlined 'Add' pill and animates its width to morph into a full '− n +' green stepper on first tap, then morphs back when decremented to zero; (2) a persistent green cart bar pinned above the tab bar showing a live item count and subtotal, entering with a spring animation on the first add; (3) an 'add-to-cart fly-up' where a ghost of the tapped product arcs toward the cart bar; (4) a per-item replacement-preference selector (best match / pick specific / don't replace) surfaced as a radio list; (5) a carrot-orange deal flag pill overlapping the top-left corner of a product photo, paired with a strikethrough original price.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Use the primary green strictly as the 'add/buy/checkout' verb color — never apply it to decorative elements or non-actionable text.
2. Use the carrot-orange accent strictly for deals, savings and sale pricing — never let it appear on a primary action button, and never swap its role with green.
3. Animate the compact 'Add' control so it visibly morphs in width into a full stepper on first tap, and morphs back to the compact form when quantity returns to zero — a static swap breaks the interaction's signature feel.
4. Keep the cart bar pinned and persistent the instant the cart contains any item — this is the core repeated loop of the product and must never be hidden or made optional.
5. Render every price, quantity and subtotal in tabular figures so multi-item lists and running totals stay vertically aligned.
6. Clamp every product title to exactly two lines with ellipsis truncation — never let a long title push the price out of its aligned column.
7. Keep unit pricing (e.g. price-per-ounce) visible in secondary gray on every product tile — treat it as a deliberate trust signal, not clutter to hide.
8. Use soft, cool-neutral, low-opacity shadows only — avoid warm or brand-colored shadow tints, and reserve the most visible elevation for the persistent cart bar alone.
9. Surface any per-item substitution/replacement choice inline and in the action-green color so the user's stated preference is visually confirmed, not buried in a settings screen.
</house_rules>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in loyalty-driven quick-service-restaurant apps with a strict two-color brand system.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles: canvas white #FFFFFF (dark #121212, never pure black), surface #F4F4F5, surface pressed #EAEAEB, divider #E3E3E5, text primary #1A1A1A, text secondary #5C5C5C. Brand red #DA291C (pressed #B71F14) drives deal flags, the secondary CTA and urgency states. Semantic support: success green #2B8A3E, warning amber #E6A700, info blue #2E6DB4.
Type ladder: one friendly, slightly-rounded humanist sans (a proprietary face; Archivo is the closest free analog) run heavy throughout — screen titles 32pt weight 900, an oversized rewards-balance numeral at 28pt/900 in the brand yellow, section headers ~19pt/800, body 16pt/400, deal titles 15pt/600, UPPERCASE badge/flag text at 12pt/800 with +0.3pt tracking. Points, prices and countdown timers are always tabular.
Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit (scale 4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-48-64); the whole system rounds generously — form fields and mode-tiles at 12pt, hero/deal cards at 16pt, bottom sheets at 20pt, and every CTA/pill/search-field at a full 999pt pill. Elevation stays mostly flat (borders/dividers define cards); the one exception is the center order button, which gets a distinctly glowing yellow-tinted shadow that makes it read as the app's single most important tap target.
Distinctive UI patterns: (1) a rewards hero card leading the home screen with an oversized yellow points number, an animated gradient progress bar, and a 'X points from Y' caption; (2) a two-up deal-tile grid, each tile a product photo with a red UPPERCASE deal flag and a 'or N points' alternate-currency line; (3) an order-mode selector offering several fulfillment methods as large tiles, the active one outlined in yellow; (4) an elevated, glowing center tab-bar button dedicated to starting an order, raised above the rest of the tab row; (5) a dashed-border coupon/deal detail card pairing a food photo with an 'add to order' yellow pill.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Enforce as an absolute, non-negotiable rule that any content placed on a yellow fill uses near-black text/icons — never white — this is the system's single hard brand law.
2. Never introduce a third loud brand color beyond the two established accents — every other surface should stay neutral so the two brand colors read clearly against it.
3. Make a loyalty/rewards balance the largest, most colorful, most prominent element on the home screen — it is the primary reason a returning user opens the app.
4. Round every actionable control (buttons, search field, status pills) to a full pill shape, and every card/sheet container to a generously large radius (16-20pt) — the whole system should read as soft and friendly, never sharp-cornered.
5. Give the single most important action in the tab bar its own elevated, glow-shadowed circular treatment distinct from the other tab items — it should visually announce itself as the primary path to conversion.
6. Set every deal flag, status badge and urgency label in UPPERCASE with a touch of positive tracking — never render these in sentence case.
7. Animate a rewards points-balance change by counting the number up and filling the progress bar from its old to new value — never let it jump instantly.
8. Offer multiple fulfillment methods (pickup, delivery, etc.) as large equally-weighted tiles rather than a dropdown, with the selected one outlined in the brand yellow.
9. Keep motion cheerful and brief (150-300ms) and always tie it to an ordering or rewards moment — never animate purely for decoration.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in booking and reservation utilities where trust and speed-to-confirm are the primary design goals.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles: canvas white #FFFFFF (dark charcoal #121212), surface #F6F6F7, surface raised #FBFBFC, divider #E4E4E7, text primary #1A1A1C, text secondary #6B6B70. A single disciplined booking accent, red #DA3743 (bright dark-mode variant #F2545B, pressed #B92C37), drives the reserve button, the selected time slot, and the active tab — nothing else. Every remaining color has exactly one job: a gold star #E8A33D for ratings only, a teal #1F8A8A for a loyalty-points program only, and a green #2FA86A for availability/social-proof messaging only.
Type ladder: one clean grotesque (a proprietary brand sans; Inter is the closest free analog) spanning weights 400 through 800 in a single family — screen titles 32pt/800, restaurant name 26pt/800, list card titles 18pt/700, body 16pt/400, and a heavy 14pt/700 for time-slot chip labels so a grid of times reads instantly.
Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit with a notably tight 9pt gap between time-slot chips so several fit one row; slot chips use a 10pt rounded-rectangle radius (not a full pill) at roughly 64pt-plus wide by 52pt tall; every button, filter chip and the search bar are a full 999pt pill; hero photography uses a 14pt radius, sheets 20pt. Elevation stays restrained and neutral throughout — a light lift (~2px/8px) on cards and the slot-grid container, a top-anchored shadow (~2px/16px) on the sticky reserve bar so it visibly floats above scrolling content.
Distinctive UI patterns: (1) a grid of rounded-rectangle time-slot chips where the recommended/selected slot fills solid brand-red and the rest stay neutral with a hairline border; (2) an optional small loyalty-points annotation beneath a slot's time, in the dedicated teal, flagging off-peak booking incentives; (3) a 'booked N times today' social-proof pill in the availability-green with a leading urgency glyph; (4) a sticky bottom bar that updates its own label to reflect the currently selected time and stays pinned through the whole detail page; (5) a restaurant card embedding a compact row of the same time-slot chips directly into the list view, not just the detail page.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Use exactly one interactive brand color for booking actions — the reserve button, the selected/recommended slot, and the active tab — and introduce no second competing action color anywhere.
2. Give every non-brand accent color exactly one job (ratings, loyalty points, availability) and never reuse it for anything else — a gold star must always mean rating, a teal must always mean points, a green must always mean availability.
3. Make the time-slot grid the visual focal point of any booking/detail screen — never bury it below the fold or de-emphasize it relative to photography or marketing copy.
4. Fill only the recommended or user-selected slot solid with the brand color; every other slot stays a neutral surface with a simple hairline border so the recommended choice is unmistakable.
5. Update a sticky bottom action bar's own label live as the user changes their selection (e.g. reflecting the chosen time) rather than leaving it generic.
6. Surface a real-time social-proof signal (e.g. recent booking volume) prominently on any detail page to build trust and urgency before the user commits.
7. Round every button, filter chip, and the search field to a full pill, but keep the time-slot chips themselves a rounded rectangle, not a pill — this distinction keeps the grid visually scannable as a grid.
8. Keep body text a neutral near-black rather than pure black, reinforcing a clean-utility rather than a stark tone.
9. Keep all transition motion brisk and restrained (150-300ms ease-out) with a soft haptic on selection — never a showy or bouncy animation for a trust-oriented booking flow.
</house_rules>
